courses.title: Investing Foundations
courses.subtitle: Start here — the free introduction
courses.description: A short, free primer on what investing actually is, the difference between a price and a value, and how the ClearGuidance terminal fits into a disciplined process. No prior finance knowledge assumed.

lessons.title: What Investing Really Is
lessons.summary: Investing as buying a claim on future cash, not betting on ticker symbols.

lessons.title: Price Is What You Pay, Value Is What You Get
lessons.summary: Why the quoted price and the underlying value are two different things.

lessons.title: How ClearGuidance Fits In
lessons.summary: Where the terminal, the models, and this Academy support your process.

courses.title: Understanding Fair Value & DCF
courses.subtitle: The flagship course
courses.description: A rigorous, self-contained walk through discounted cash flow valuation — the framework the ClearGuidance terminal is built on. You will learn where fair value comes from, how each assumption moves it, how to read the outputs honestly, and when a DCF is the wrong tool. Each concept links to the live terminal for hands-on reinforcement.

lessons.title: Why Fair Value Exists
lessons.summary: The idea that a business has an intrinsic worth independent of its quote.

lessons.title: The Margin of Safety
lessons.summary: Buying below value as protection against error and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Cash Flows and the Time Value of Money
lessons.summary: Why a dollar tomorrow is worth less than a dollar today.

lessons.title: The Growth Rate
lessons.summary: How projected earnings growth drives — and distorts — fair value.

lessons.title: The Discount Rate
lessons.summary: The required return that reflects risk and the time value of money.

lessons.title: The Terminal Multiple
lessons.summary: Capturing value beyond the explicit forecast horizon.

lessons.title: Base DCF vs. Your DCF
lessons.summary: The institutional baseline versus your custom scenario.

lessons.title: Upside, Downside, and Honest Interpretation
lessons.summary: Reading the gap between price and fair value without fooling yourself.

lessons.title: The Sensitivity Matrix
lessons.summary: Seeing how fair value shifts across ranges of assumptions.

lessons.title: The Confidence Gauge
lessons.summary: What the gauge measures — assumption aggressiveness, not certainty of return.

lessons.title: DCF Suitability and the Analyst Range
lessons.summary: A separate signal: is a DCF even the right tool here, and what wide analyst spreads tell you.

lessons.title: Negative Earnings and the Revenue-Driven Model
lessons.summary: Why unprofitable companies need a different valuation approach.

lessons.title: The Limits of DCF
lessons.summary: Where the model is fragile and how to use it responsibly.

courses.title: Reading the Chart
courses.subtitle: Price, levels, and timing
courses.description: A DCF tells you what a business is worth; the chart tells you what the market is doing about it right now. This course teaches the price-action side of the terminal — support, resistance, the point of control, and sentiment — and how to combine a margin-of-safety entry with sensible timing. Every concept links to the live chart for hands-on reinforcement.

lessons.title: Support: Where Demand Shows Up
lessons.summary: Why prices tend to stop falling at certain levels, and how the terminal draws support.

lessons.title: Resistance: Where Supply Caps Price
lessons.summary: The mirror image of support — where sellers repeatedly cap advances.

lessons.title: When Levels Break — and Flip
lessons.summary: Breakouts, false breaks, and why broken support often becomes new resistance.

lessons.title: Point of Control: The Volume Magnet
lessons.summary: The single most-traded price and why it tends to pull price back toward it.

lessons.title: Reading Market Sentiment
lessons.summary: What the bullish / bearish / neutral read means and how to weigh it against your valuation.

lessons.title: Putting It Together: Value Meets Timing
lessons.summary: Combining a margin-of-safety entry with support, resistance, and sentiment.
